title: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Playbook (Supplement)
author: Michael Chen
summary: Supplemental playbook consolidating budgeting & forecasting rhythms, procurement and contract approval flows, and revenue recognition + billing operational guidance. Designed for finance, legal, procurement, product and engineering stakeholders to ensure consistent, auditable execution.
overview: Purpose: Provide a single-reference operational playbook for quarterly budgeting and forecasting, vendor procurement and contracting, purchase order (PO) controls, and revenue recognition/billing mechanics (aligned to ASC 606 principles). This supplement clarifies thresholds, owners, and operational checklists that augment the main Finance Playbook.
scope: Applies to all Redwood Inference entities and business units. Includes hosted API, Dedicated, and Private product lines. Excludes M&A-specific contracting (see Contracts M&A appendix).
roles_and_responsibilities:
- VP Finance: final sign-off on annual operating plan (AOP) and headcount envelope above $1M.
- Finance Business Partner (FBP): maintain forecast cadence, variance analysis, monthly revenue reconciliation.
- Legal: contract review for terms, liability caps, data handling provisions, and privacy clauses.
- Procurement: vendor onboarding, PO issuance, supplier risk assessment.
- Procurement Committee: approves strategic vendor spend > $250k or multi-year contracts.
- Product/Engineering Managers: provide capacity forecasts, resource plans, and SOW acceptance.
- Sales/RevOps: owns invoicing cadence policies and commercial changes that impact billing.
budgeting_and_forecasting_process:
Quarterly and annual process overview:
1) Annual Operating Plan (AOP) (Oct–Dec): Finance leads AOP submissions; business units submit target-based budgets with assumptions (traffic, ARR growth, seat-based pricing, hosting cost per token).
2) Quarterly Forecast Updates (Q-5, Q-3, Q-1): FBPs collect rolling 12-month forecasts; each update must include headcount delta, committed contracts, and material vendor changes.
3) Monthly Forecast Reconciliation: FBPs produce MTD/MTD variance, backlog, deferred revenue movements, and gross margin by product line by 7th business day.
Acceptance criteria and controls:
- All variance > 10% YTD must include root-cause narrative and remediation plan.
- Headcount changes that increase annual run-rate > $150k require VP Finance approval.
Tools and outputs:
- Forecast file: finance/forecasts/<BU>-rolling-12.csv (canonical), uploaded to Financial Drive.
- Approval workflow executed in FinanceWorkflow (internal tool) with audit trail.
- Key deliverables: AOP workbook, Budget vs Forecast dashboard, Headcount plan, Cash runway model.
procurement_and_contracts_process:
High-level procurement workflow:
1) Need identification: Requester (PM/Eng) completes Purchase Request (PR) with business justification, budget code, and estimated total cost.
2) Procurement intake: Procurement validates budget availability and risk category.
3) Competitive sourcing: For expected spend > $100k, procurement must solicit at least 3 bids (exceptions documented). For strategic/unique vendors, Procurement Committee approval required.
4) Contracting: Legal reviews master services agreements (MSA), data processing addenda (DPA), and security questionnaires. Standard redlines exist for common vendor types (SaaS, Infrastructure, Consulting).
5) PO issuance & payment: Upon signature, Procurement issues PO and Finance schedules payment terms in AP system.
Contract review thresholds (summary table):
| Contract Type | Estimated Annual Value | Legal Review | Procurement Committee | Security Review |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Standard SaaS | <$50k | Standard Templated Review | No | Security questionnaire if vendor stores customer data |
| Strategic SaaS / Infra | $50k-$250k | Legal full review | Procurement notified | Formal security assessment (3rd-party report) |
| High-value / Multi-year | >$250k | Legal + Exec Review | Yes (committee) | SOC2/ISO27001 + penetration test report preferred |
Escalation and approval matrix (text):
- PO <$10k: Requester manager approves.
- PO $10k-$50k: Director of Requester approves and Procurement logs vendor onboarding.
- PO $50k-$250k: VP Finance and Procurement approval required.
- PO > $250k: Procurement Committee + VP Finance + Legal sign-off.
Vendor onboarding requirements:
- Completed vendor intake form, tax/W-9 documentation, AML/KYC where applicable, security attestation, and contract template selection.
- For vendors with access to customer data or production systems, complete security review (Security team SLA: 10 business days) and obtain a Data Processing Addendum signed by vendor.
Standard contracting notes:
- Use Redwood Master Services Agreement (MSA) as baseline. Do not sign vendor-supplied MSA without Legal approval.
- Liability caps default to 12 months of fees unless Legal approves higher exposure.
- Data residency or export controls must be explicitly captured in the DPA and reviewed by Security/Legal.
purchase_order_and_payment_controls:
PO/purchasing controls checklist:
- Every commercial commitment must have an approved PR/PO prior to vendor work commencing, except in documented emergency spend.
- AP payment terms default to Net 30 unless negotiated otherwise by Finance.
- Capital vs expense treatment: Finance will adjudicate accounting treatment at time of invoice based on asset class and capitalization thresholds (capex threshold: $10k per asset).
- One-time exceptions require email approval from VP Finance and retention of approval in Procurement record.
revenue_recognition_and_billing_policy:
Principles (ASC 606-aligned):
1) Identify the contract with the customer: Signed MSA/SOW or accepted order.
2) Identify performance obligations: e.g., hosted API access, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private deployment license + support, professional services.
3) Determine transaction price: include variable consideration estimates (usage, credits, discounts).
4) Allocate transaction price to performance obligations.
5) Recognize revenue when performance obligation is satisfied (over time or at a point in time).
Operational guidance:
- Subscription/commit contracts: Recognize ratably over the contract term unless deliverable tied to discrete milestone (e.g., on-prem install accepted by customer).
- Usage billing: Recognize as usage occurs; deferred revenue recognized monthly based on measured consumption.
- Professional services: Recognize based on milestone and acceptance criteria. If services are distinct, recognize upon delivery and customer acceptance; if bundled, allocate transaction price accordingly.
- Credits and refunds: Treated as contra-revenue; estimate accruals for expected credits using historical run rates and contract terms.
Billing & collections:
- Standard invoice cadence: Monthly in arrears for usage and subscription unless contract specifies otherwise. Net terms default to Net 30.
- Invoicing system: RevOps issues invoices via BillingPlatform (internal). Disputes logged in BillingPlatform with SLA: billing team acknowledges within 3 business days, resolution target 15 business days.
Deferred revenue and month-end close:
- Finance must run deferred revenue roll-forward each month and reconcile to GL account 2300.
- Any contract modifications affecting scope/term must be evaluated for reallocation of transaction price and adjusted prospectively/retrospectively per ASC 606; document rationale and accounting treatment in the Contract Accounting Workpaper.
Revenue cutoff controls:
- Cutoff tests: verify shipments (or service acceptance) recorded in the correct month; usage-based records must be captured with timestamped logs.
- Sales credits > $25k require Finance approval and must be recorded in the appropriate month with an explanation.
auditing_and_compliance:
- Retention: Contracts and procurement records retained for 7 years.
- Internal audits: Finance runs a semi-annual procurement and revrec control audit; findings tracked in AuditTracker.
- External audits: Provide SOC2 and revenue support packages during annual audit; responsible owners must prepare Contract Accounting Workpapers within 10 business days of request.
- Compliance: Ensure KYC/AML checks for international vendors and cross-border data transfer controls for Private deployments.
incident_and_dispute_escalation:
Billing dispute process:
1) Customer opens dispute via support portal; RevOps creates a dispute ticket and assigns to Billing team.
2) Billing team investigates with Sales and Engineering as needed.
3) Interim credit may be issued for confirmed errors; permanent adjustments require Finance approval.
Contract breaches or vendor performance issues:
- For vendor SLA breaches, Procurement engages vendor and Legal; for material breaches, Procurement Committee evaluates remedies including termination, service credits, or litigation hold.
- Escalation contacts: VP Finance (finance@redwood.ai), Head of Legal (legal@redwood.ai), Procurement Director (procurement@redwood.ai).
appendix_tables_and_checklists:
Approval matrix (ASCII table):
| Approval Type | Threshold | Approver | Record Location | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| PO approval | <$10k | Manager | Procurement Portal | Auto-approved if budget exists |
| PO approval | $10k-$50k | Director | Procurement Portal | Budget check required |
| PO approval | $50k-$250k | VP Finance + Procurement | Procurement Portal + FinanceWorkflow | Legal loop if contract involved |
| PO approval | >$250k | Procurement Committee + VP Finance + Legal | Procurement Portal + CLM | Board notification if > $1M |
Vendor onboarding checklist:
- Completed vendor intake form
- Tax documentation (W-9/appropriate local form)
- Security questionnaire completed or SOC2/ISO report obtained
- Signed MSA/DPA in CLM
- PO issued and in AP system
Monthly revenue close checklist:
- Deferred revenue roll-forward completed and reconciled to GL
- Unbilled receivables evaluated and supported by usage logs/SOWs
- Contract modifications recorded and accounted for
- Revenue waterfall for enterprise deals (> $250k) reviewed by Controller
Sample contract redline priorities (high level):
1) Data protection and DPA terms
2) Liability cap and indemnities
3) Confidentiality and IP ownership
4) Termination for convenience and transition support
5) Audit rights and subcontracting clauses
